card.occupation: Clinical trials coordinator in the research unit of an NHS teaching hospital in East London. She schedules patient visits, keeps trial paperwork audit-ready, processes samples for courier and enters data into the trial databases.
card.education_detail: Bachelor's degree in Biology from Masaryk University in Brno, Czech Republic. Since moving to the UK she has added a Good Clinical Practice certificate and a short online course in clinical research coordination.
card.household: Lives with her husband Tom, 32, a British-born electrician, in a rented two-bedroom flat above a row of shops near Leyton High Road. They married three years ago at a register office in Walthamstow and had a second small party in Brno. They have no children yet. The second bedroom is half office, half spare room for when her mum visits.
card.cultural_background: Grew up in Brno in the Czech Republic, the daughter of a secondary-school maths teacher and a tram depot mechanic. She has one younger brother, who still lives there. The family wasn't religious, and neither is she, though she keeps Czech Christmas traditions out of habit and nostalgia: carp, potato salad, cookies baked weeks ahead. She came to London at 22, intending to stay a year, and has now been here eight. She speaks Czech with family on the phone most evenings and feels somewhere between the two countries.
card.professional_persona: Meticulous and quietly relied upon. She is the person who notices the missing signature on a consent form before the monitor does. She keeps colour-coded checklists and gets visibly tense before audits, but her files are always in order. She is good with nervous patients because she is a bit of a worrier herself, and she explains things slowly and kindly.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. She swims at Leyton Leisure Lagoon a couple of early mornings a week, does a beginners' yoga class on Thursdays, and walks a lot on Walthamstow Marshes and around Lea Bridge. She'll watch ice hockey when Czechia is in the World Championship, and gets far more emotional about it than she expects to.
card.arts_persona: Reads a lot, mostly Scandinavian crime novels and some literary fiction in both English and Czech, and belongs to a small book club at the local library. She likes the Barbican cinema and the occasional West End play when there are cheap tickets. She cries easily at films and doesn't hide it.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Brno twice a year, usually by plane, though she's a nervous flyer and grips the armrest on take-off. She prefers planned trips with booked accommodation to anything spontaneous. Favourite holidays have been a walking week in the Lake District and a long weekend in Porto with Tom.
card.culinary_persona: A competent, organised home cook who batch-cooks on Sundays and labels the freezer boxes. She makes svíčková when she's homesick and bakes a lot. Tom has converted her to a proper roast and Friday fish and chips. She calls the evening meal dinner, and does the big shop at Lidl with a list.
hobbies_and_interests: baking, especially Czech pastries and cakes
book club at the local library
growing tomatoes and herbs in pots on the small back balcony
card.career_goals: To move up to a senior clinical research coordinator or clinical research associate role within the next few years. She has been looking at a part-time master's in clinical research, but worries about fitting it in with work and maybe starting a family.
card.voice: Fluent English with a soft Czech accent that she's slightly self-conscious about. She sometimes drops an article ('I went to shop') or puts stress in unexpected places, and she corrects herself with a quick 'sorry, I mean...'. Her pace is moderate and careful when she's thinking, quicker when she's enthusiastic. She uses 'erm' and 'sort of' a fair bit and has picked up 'knackered', 'mate' and 'to be honest' from Tom and her colleagues. She ends points with 'you know?' or 'yeah?' to check she's understood. She doesn't like long silences and will fill them with a nervous little laugh or 'erm, does that make sense?'
card.typing: Types properly even in a hurry: capital letters, full stops, correct apostrophes. She rarely abbreviates beyond 'e.g.' or 'etc.' and sometimes reads her answer back before submitting. The occasional small slip shows English isn't her first language, such as a missing 'the' or 'since five years' instead of 'for five years'.
card.with_strangers: Polite, warm and a little reserved at first. She apologises more than she needs to and is anxious to give the 'right' answer. Once she relaxes she's chatty and funny, especially about the cultural differences between Czech and British life.
small_things: her tomato plants on the balcony and whether the pigeons will get them
the Central line being too hot in summer
the cake she baked for a colleague's leaving do
how cheap the Lidl on the High Road is compared with the big supermarkets
being knackered after an early swim
deeper_things: worrying about her mum, who had a health scare last year and lives far away
feeling not fully at home in either country, and the paperwork stress she went through for settled status after Brexit
the question of whether and when to have children, and whether to raise them in London or nearer family
an anxious streak she manages with routines and lists
missing her grandmother, who died during the pandemic when she couldn't travel back
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, head and shoulders, slightly from below because the laptop sits on a desk. Soft daylight from a window to her left, so the left side of her face is brighter. She has light brown hair tied in a low, slightly messy bun with a few strands loose, grey-green eyes, fair skin, light freckles across the nose, and no makeup apart from a little mascara. She wears thin gold-rimmed round glasses and a small polite smile with eyebrows slightly raised, as if waiting to be spoken to. She's dressed in a navy knitted jumper over a white T-shirt collar and small silver stud earrings. Behind her is a white wall in the spare room with a cork board pinned with a printed calendar, a few postcards and a photo of her and Tom at their wedding. To the right is a narrow bookshelf with paperbacks, a couple of Czech titles and a basil plant in a pot. In the corner, the end of a single folded-up spare bed is covered with a grey throw.
